subject: Blackbox exclusion and custodial output rights for HealthIQ pilot
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthiq.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Blackbox exclusion & output custody for HealthIQ pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthIQ is excited to pilot Redwood for our member triage flows. Before we spin up inference traffic, legal has a couple of hard requirements we need confirmed in writing: 

- A contractual commitment that HealthIQ data will not be used to improve or retrain any model (we need an auditable statement of "no model improvement" on our data).
- Explicit custody/ownership language that makes HealthIQ the owner of prompt/response outputs generated during our tenant sessions.
- Operational evidence: how we get a sandboxed copy of interactions for our archive (SFTP export preferred) and a simple proof-of-non-learning flow to share with our compliance team.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Provide a standing no-improvement clause and associated evidence package?
2) Offer tenant-scoped SFTP export (EU region preferred) for on-demand snapshots and an audit log showing no downstream model transfers?

Ben from our legal team is cc'd. If you have a short checklist or one-pager we can circulate internally, that would help accelerate procurement.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Product & Partnerships
HealthIQ

[Attachment: HealthIQ_Request_Summary.docx (docx)]

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthiq.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Blackbox exclusion & output custody for HealthIQ pilot

Hi Claire — great to hear and thanks for spelling this out. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short checklist and evidence artifacts in a separate email.

1) No-model-improvement commitment: Yes — Redwood supports a contractual prohibition on using customer inputs/responses to improve hosted models. We can add explicit DPA language that:
   - Prohibits use of HealthIQ data for model training, fine-tuning, or human-in-the-loop model improvement.
   - Commits to operational controls (ephemeral KV cache policies, restricted telemetry retention for the pilot).

2) Custodial ownership of outputs: We can include language that grants HealthIQ explicit ownership/licensing of prompts and generated outputs produced under your tenant for the term of the agreement.

3) Operational evidence & SFTP export: We offer tenant-scoped SFTP export for EU residency customers. For the pilot we can:
   - Provision an EU-resident SFTP bucket for nightly snapshots (or on-demand export).
   - Provide an evidence pack (audit log excerpt + S3/SFTP transfer receipt) showing export files and retention metadata.

Next steps I propose:
- I will attach a 1-page "pilot checklist" and our standard DPA excerpt for no-training language.
- David (privacy) will confirm the exact audit artifacts we can supply.
- Marissa (CS) will coordinate an ops timeline and biweekly check-ins.

Would Tuesday 11/11 11:00am PT work for a short call to align on the checklist?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: HealthIQ_Pilot_Checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: david_kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthiq.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Blackbox exclusion & output custody for HealthIQ pilot

Soojin / Claire — quick technical clarification from privacy/ops perspective so we set expectations correctly.

- No-training evidence: We can provide a signed DPA excerpt committing to no-model-improvement and a runtime audit excerpt showing that requests from the HealthIQ tenant were routed to an instance with training disabled. Evidence artifacts we can supply:
   * Signed DPA section (legal)
   * Runtime request routing log showing tenant ID and instance IDs for a 7-day sample
   * KV cache policy config (ephemeral) showing retention TTLs

- Export mechanisms: Two viable paths for the pilot (both EU-resident):
   1) SFTP nightly snapshot — good for batch archival and a simple transfer receipt. We will provide the SFTP host, file manifest, and checksum.
   2) API-driven on-demand export — JSONL with per-interaction metadata (timestamp, request_id, model_variant, response_hash).

- Escrow for outputs: We do not hold customer outputs in third-party escrow by default, but we can support an escrow arrangement as part of procurement (we've done this in select enterprise deals). That would be a procurement add-on — legal will need to route escrow docs and attestations.

I'll attach the ops playbook for the SFTP path and a short checklist of log artifacts we can provide.

Regards,
David Kim
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sftp_onboarding_steps.md (text)]

Thanks David — that helps. Two follow-ups from legal and security: 

- Legal would like a short contract amendment that explicitly lists the evidence artifacts (routing logs, export receipts, retention policy) and commits Redwood to provide those artifacts within X business days of request. Can Redwood commit to 5 business days?
- Security asks for a signed statement that tenant traffic will be segregated and that there will be no cross-tenant model updates touching our data. A short attestation PDF would be ideal.

Also, for the escrow option — can you outline typical timelines and costs? Procurement will need that to evaluate.

We'd like the SFTP option and EU residency for exports; please confirm the hostname and whether keys will be customer-managed.

If you can send a simple doc that procurement/legal can sign off on (1-pager + sample contract language), we'll push this through.

Best,
Claire
